note: Two streamside sites about 310 m apart on Left Branch Young Womans Creek Road near Shingle Branch: site 023 is the first after the Shingle Branch bridge and site 024 the second, on the right. The booking calendar read 2026-11-10 offers neither site before 2 July 2027 and gives no reason. DCNR has closed the road indefinitely from its junction with Young Womans Creek Road, gated and locked at the state forest boundary, because its southern part crosses private land; the forest beyond can be reached only from the north, so the booking pages' directions from North Bend no longer work. Campers must bring a self-contained toilet. The agency cautions that it is reached by remote dirt or gravel forest roads that may not suit low-clearance vehicles or large RVs. No table or water. Pack out trash. --Claude
summary: Both site pages re-read: 023 and 024 Shingle Branch still listed, Drive-In, Trailer Site category, max vehicle 25 ft, parallel gravel, spur 35 ft; count 2 and 25 ft confirmed, pull_through false and a sites note added (024 equipment length 15). flags: STATUS (ruling 6 applied): calendars for both sites read 'Not Available' on every night of the windows from 2026-11-17, 2026-12-01, 2027-02-15, 2027-03-15, 2027-04-15, 2027-05-12, 2027-05-26, 2027-06-09 and 2027-06-23; the first Available night is 2027-07-02, and the 2027-07-14 and 2027-09-15 windows are fully Available. The site pages give no reason and still say 'Status: Open year round'. Written status temporarily_closed with reopens '2 July 2027 per the booking calendar'.

Road closure: Sproul advisories page: 'The Left Branch Young Woman's Creek Road will be closed indefinitely beginning at the intersection of Young Woman's Creek Rd. ... gated and locked at the state forest boundary. Visitors can only access the road and state forest acreage in this region from the north. The southern portion of the road rests on private land ... Currently, the public is not permitted through the private area.' The DCNR gate map (June 26, 2025) shows two gates on the road, one at the state forest boundary about half a mile north of the fork and one at Mudlick Run about 1.2 miles north of the fork (distances scaled from the map by eye, not agency figures); both sites lie north of both gates. The site pages still direct campers from PA 120 at North Bend up Main Street, Right Branch Young Womans Creek Road and 'bear left onto Left Branch Young Womans Creek Road' 2.3 miles (023) / 2.5 miles (024). No page read links the calendar block to the road closure or names the northern approach road; the link is not stated by the agency.

Figures: site 024 Shingle Branch has 'Max Vehicle Length: 25' beside 'Equipment Length: 15' (site 40 x 50 ft, spur 35 ft, five people). Max Vehicle Length is 23 ft or more but Equipment Length is under 23 ft: kept in the count with the figures in the sites note. Site 023 is 25/25.

NHD: 023 is 25 m from Shingle Branch; 024 is 120 m from Left Branch Young Womans Creek. Agency access statements (ruling 11: nothing measured, no road surface, gate or bridge research): 'Caution: This campsite is accessed by remote state forest dirt or gravel roads and may not be suitable for some low-clearance vehicles or large RVs.' No grade lines, no Severe grade, no site-specific 4WD or wet-weather statement; overhead clearance 20 ft on both. Kept. Boilerplate on every page of the district, not site-specific: 'State forest roads are not maintained in the winter and often become snow covered, icy and potentially impassable' and '4WD vehicles may be recommended for some sites year-round, check notes' (this site's notes say nothing about 4WD).
